{{ill|Takehi-Nateru|ja|建比良鳥命|en:draft|Takehi-Nateru}} (建比良鳥命) is a Japanese god and son of {{ill|Ame no Hohi|en|Ame no Hohi}},<ref name="web.archive.org-2023">{{Cite web|date=2023-03-21|title=Takehiratori {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230321165525/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9146|access-date=2024-03-24|website=web.archive.org}}</ref><ref name="web.archive.org-2023a">{{Cite web|date=2023-06-05|title=Amenohohi {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230605104153/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9434|access-date=2024-03-24|website=web.archive.org}}</ref><ref name="shintoshrines">{{Cite web|title=The Gods of Japan {{!}} Amaterasu-Ōkami 天照大御神 {{!}}Susanoo-no-Mikoto 須佐之男命|url=https://www.rodsshinto.com/amasusa|access-date=2024-03-24|website=shintoshrines|language=en}}</ref><ref name="More glimpses of unfamiliar Japan">{{Cite web|title=More glimpses of unfamiliar Japan|url=https://www.ojisanjake.com/2014/03/|access-date=2024-03-24|language=en}}</ref><ref name="英訳 出雲神話">{{Cite web|title=英訳 出雲神話/English Translation Izumo Myths::２．天の安の河の誓約-出雲神話翻訳研究会/The Man From Izumo tells the Izumo-myths of the Kojiki|url=http://izumo-kojiki.com/izumomyths/amaterasu/100/|access-date=2024-03-24|language=ja}}</ref> one of the five male kami (divine beings) born from a special event known as the "trial by pledge" between two major deities, Amaterasu and Susanoo. {{ill|Ame no Hohi|en|Ame no Hohi}} was sent to the {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|en|fr}}'''|葦原の中つ国|''The middle country of {{ill|reed bed|en|reed bed|lt=reed beds}}''}} to prepare for the {{ill|Tenson kōrin|en|Tenson kōrin|lt=Tenson korin}}.<ref name="web.archive.org-2023" />

He is the ancestor of many prominent families in, {{ill|Izumo Province|en|Izumo Province|qid=Q582846|lt=Izumo}}, {{ill|Musashi Province|en|Musashi Province|qid=Q907398|lt=Musashi}}, {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|en|Chiba Prefecture|qid=Q80011|lt=Chiba}}, and {{ill|Tsushima Province|en|Tsushima Province|qid=Q1054861|lt=Tsushima}}.<ref name="shintoshrines" /><ref name="英訳 出雲神話" /> He started the Fire fesival of [[Izumo-taisha]].<ref name="Brown-1988" />

Ame no Hohi's other son is {{ill|Ame no Wakahiko|en|Ame no Wakahiko}}.<ref name="Brown-1988">{{Cite book |last1=Brown |first1=Delmer M. |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/The_Cambridge_History_of_Japan/A3_6lp8IOK8C?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=Ame+no+Hohi&pg=PA346&printsec=frontcover |title=The Cambridge History of Japan |last2=Hall |first2=John Whitney |last3=Brown |first3=Delmer Myers |last4=Press |first4=Cambridge University |last5=Jansen |first5=Marius B. |last6=McCullough |first6=William H. |last7=Shively |first7=Donald H. |last8=Yamamura |first8=Kozo |last9=Duus |first9=Peter |date=1988 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-0-521-22352-2 |pages=346 |language=en}}</ref> He is also known by the name {{ill|Takehi-Nateru|en|Takehi-Nateru|lt=Ame-no-Hinadori}}, contrary to popular belief that is not the name of an additional son.<ref name="web.archive.org-2023" /> 

== Names ==
Takehi-Nateru, also known by several other names such as Takehiratori no Mikoto, Takehinatori no Mikoto, and Ame no Hinatori.<ref name="web.archive.org-2023" />

== Role in Mythology ==
In the Kojiki, the oldest Japanese book, Takehi-Nateru is mentioned as an ancestor to the [[Izumo clan|Izumo no Kuni no Miyatsuko]]. Both the [[Kojiki]] and [[Nihon Shoki]], narrate how {{ill|Ame no Hohi|en|Ame no Hohi}} was tasked with preparing the {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|fa|آشیهارا نو ناکاتسوکونی|fr|Ashihara no nakatsukuni|it|Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|ja|葦原中国|ko|위원중국|pl|Kraj Pośród Uprawnych Pól|ru|Асихара-но Накацукуни|th|อาชิฮาระ โนะ นากัตสึกูนิ|zh|葦原中國|qid=Q1096244}}'''|葦原の中つ国|''The middle country of {{ill|Reed bed|ar|مقصبة|bat_smg|Lėndrīns|be|Плаўні|be_x_old|Плаўні|ca|Canyissar|cs|Rákosina|da|Rørsump|de|Röhricht|el|Καλαμιώνας|eo|Kareksejo|es|Juncal|et|Roostik|eu|Lezkadi|fa|نیزار|fr|Roselière|hu|Nádasok|id|Padang rumput buluh|it|Canneto (ecologia)|ja|ヨシ原|lt|Nendrynas|lv|Klāni|nl|Rietland|pl|Szuwar|pt|Canavial|ru|Плавни|simple|Reed bed|sl|Trstičevje|sv|Vass (vegetation)|tr|Sazlık|uk|Плавні|wa|Rozire (ecolodjeye)|zh|蘆原|qid=Q620424|lt=Reed bed}}s''|qq=draft}} but ultimately did not succeed in his mission.<ref name="web.archive.org-2023" />

So Takehi-Nateru and {{ill|Futsunushi|en|Futsunushi}} went down to pacify {{ill|Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|fa|آشیهارا نو ناکاتسوکونی|fr|Ashihara no nakatsukuni|it|Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|ja|葦原中国|ko|위원중국|pl|Kraj Pośród Uprawnych Pól|ru|Асихара-но Накацукуни|th|อาชิฮาระ โนะ นากัตสึกูนิ|zh|葦原中國|qid=Q1096244}}. They managed to subdue unruly deities and persuaded a prominent deity, [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi]], to leave the earthly realm. After their victory the heavenly grandchild [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ninigi]] descended to the Earth and Takehi-Nateru became the ancestor of the [[Izumo clan|Izumo no Kuni no Miyatsuko]], who ruled {{ill|Izumo Province|en|Izumo Province|qid=Q582846|lt=Izumo Province}}.<ref name="web.archive.org-2023" />

== Legacy ==
According to the Nihongi's account of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|qid=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sujin}}, Takehi-Nateru descended from heaven with divine treasures.<ref name="Brown-1988" /><ref name="web.archive.org-2023" /> These treasures were kept at [[Izumo-taisha]] and later handed over to the {{ill|Emperor of Japan|en|Emperor of Japan|qid=Q208233|lt=Emperor of Japan}}. However, this transfer led to conflicts among the Izumo, Furune, and Iiirine family branches, who were the keepers of these sacred items. Today, shrines in {{ill|Izumo Province|en|Izumo Province|qid=Q582846|lt=Izumo}} and {{ill|Inaba Province|en|Inaba Province|qid=Q1054338|lt=Inaba}} honor Takehi-Nateru.<ref name="web.archive.org-2023" />
